newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Brent offerings dry up, but arb promises more.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Brent offerings dry up, but arb promises more.

text.p: Brent offerings on the U.S. Gulf Coast dried up on Friday amid growing refinery demand in the Mediterranean and the Far East, but the wide arbitrage promised to generate more, traders said.
A European major on Thursday sold the last of five Brent cargoes into the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP).
A U.S. refinery bought the cargo for a discount of $1.27 to benchmark June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for May 8-12 delivery.
Earlier in the week, a trading house had been assessing interest in delivering Brent into the Gulf at the end of May for around June WTI/Cushing minus 85 cents a barrel.
The spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.70-75 a barrel Friday afternoon.
Among more obscure UK crudes, a U.S. refiner was offering onshore crude Wyche Farm for June WTI/Cushing minus 60 cents a barrel delivered around May 18-22, traders said.

From West Africa, Tosco Corp on Friday purchased two million barrels of Nigerian Qua Iboe for early May delivery to its shuttered Trainer, Pa., refinery, and mainstay Bayway facility in New Jersey, traders said.
Market sources said the shipment of West African crude to the Trainer facility did not alter Tosco's plans to restart the idled plant in early summer.
Traders said the Qua Iboe sale was for two cargoes of one million barrels each for dated Brent plus 22 cents fob.
Elsewhere in the region, a U.S. company was offering Angolan Palanca crude for end-May arrival, asking June WTI/Cushing minus 40 cents a barrel.

In Latin America, Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) bought 900,000 barrels of Nigerian Forcados and 380,000 barrels of Ecuadoran Oriente in its latest crude oil purchase tender, trade sources said.
A variable of plus or minus 10 percent was agreed on the Oriente volume, the sources said.
The cargoes will be delivered between the end of May and early June.

The prices for the transactions were not disclosed. Traders said the Forcados was pegged to either benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing or dated Brent, while Oriente was sold at a discount to WTI.
Elsewhere, an Argentine company was offering 380,000 barrels of Canadon Seco crude for loading May 10-11, trade sources said.
On Thursday, an equity producer sold a Colombian Cusiana cargo for May 22-23 delivery at WTI/Cushing minus $1.56 a barrel, trade sources said.
